source_text: XV. Ταῦτα δὲ αὐτοῦ λαλήσαντος καὶ ἐπισπουδάσαντος αὐτοὺς ἐξελθεῖν ἐκ τῆς φυλακῆς ἐπέστησαν αὐτοῖς ὁ νεωκόρος Πολέμων καὶ ὁ ἵππαρχος Θεόφιλος μετὰ διωγμιτῶν καὶ ὄχλου πολλοῦ λέγοντες· Ἰδοὺ Εὐκτήμων ὁ προεστὼς ὑμῶν ἐπέθυσεν, πείσθητε καὶ ὑμεῖς· ἐρωτῶσιν ὑμᾶς Λέπιδος καὶ Εὐκτήμων ἐν τῷ Νεμεσείῳ. Πιόνιος εἶπεν· Τοὺς βληθέντας εἰς τὴν φυλακὴν ἀκόλουθόν ἐστι περιμένειν τὸν ἀνθύπατον· τί ἑαυτοῖς τὰ ἐκείνου μέρη ἐπιτρέπετε; Ἀπῆλθον οὖν πολλὰ εἰπόντες, καὶ πάλιν ἦλθον μετὰ διωγμιτῶν καὶ ὄχλου, καί φησι Θεόφιλος ὁ ἵππαρχος δόλῳ· Πέπομφεν ὁ ἀνθύπατος ἵνα εἰς Ἔφεσον ἀπαχθῆτε. Πιόνιος εἶπεν· Ἐλθέτω ὁ πεμφθεὶς καὶ παραλαβέτω ἡμᾶς. Ὁ ἵππαρχος εἶπεν· Ἀλλὰ πρίγκιψ ἐστὶν ἀξιόλογος· εἰ δὲ οὐ θέλεις, ἄρχων εἰμί. Καὶ ἐπιλαβόμενος αὐτοῦ ἔσφιγξε τὸ μαφόριον περὶ τὸν τράχηλον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐπέδωκε διωγμίτῃ, ὡς μικροῦ δεῖν αὐτὸν πνῖξαι. Ἐξῆλθον οὖν εἰς τὴν ἀγορὰν καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ καὶ ἡ Σαβῖνα, καὶ κράζοντων αὐτῶν μεγάλῃ φωνῇ Χριστιανοί ἐσμεν, καὶ χαμαὶ ῥιπτόντων ἑαυτοὺς πρὸς τὸ μὴ ἀπενεχθῆναι εἰς τὸ εἰδωλεῖον, οἱ διωγμῖται τὸν Πιόνιον ἐβάσταζον κατὰ κεφαλῆς, ὡς μὴ δυναμένους κατέχειν αὐτὸν τοῖς γόνασι λακτίζειν εἰς τὰς πλευρὰς καὶ τὰς χεῖρας καὶ τοὺς πόδας αὐτῶν ὀχλάσαι.
pass_a_gloss: While he was saying these things and urging them to come out of the prison, Polemon the temple-warden and Theophilus the hipparch stood over them with diogmitai and a large crowd, saying: Behold Euktemon your head has sacrificed, be persuaded also you; Lepidus and Euktemon ask for you in the Nemeseion. Pionius said: For those thrown into prison it is fitting to wait for the proconsul; why do you take upon yourselves his functions? They went away therefore having said many things, and came again with diogmitai and crowd, and Theophilus the hipparch says by deceit: The proconsul has sent that you be led away to Ephesus. Pionius said: Let the one sent come and receive us. The hipparch said: But he is a princeps of account; if you do not wish it, I am a magistrate. And laying hold of him he tightened the maphorion around his neck and gave him to a diogmites, so as nearly to choke him. They went out therefore into the marketplace, both the rest and Sabina, and while they were crying with a loud voice We are Christians, and throwing themselves to the ground so as not to be carried off into the idol-temple, the diogmitai were carrying Pionius head-foremost, since they were unable to hold him, kicking with the knees into the sides and forcing the hands and feet to bend.
pass_b_english: While he was still speaking these words and urging them to leave the prison, Polemon the keeper of the temple and Theophilus the commander of horse came upon them with their trackers and a great crowd, saying, See, Euctemon your leader has sacrificed; let yourselves be persuaded as well.
Lepidus and Euctemon are asking for you at the sanctuary of Nemesis.
Pionius said, Those who have been cast into prison ought to wait for the proconsul; why do you take his office upon yourselves?
So after many words they went away, and came back again with trackers and crowd, and Theophilus the commander said by a trick, The proconsul has sent orders for you to be taken to Ephesus.
Pionius said, Let the man who was sent come and take charge of us.
The commander said, But he is a princeps of rank; and if you refuse, I am a magistrate.
Then seizing him he drew his veil tight about his throat and handed him to a tracker, so that he nearly choked him.

So the rest came out into the marketplace, and Sabina with them, and while they cried with a loud voice, We are Christians, and cast themselves down upon the ground so as not to be borne off to the house of idols, the trackers lifted and bore Pionius head foremost, and since they could not get a grip on him, they kicked his sides with their knees and went crouching on their own hands and feet.

lemmas.gloss: to force to crouch or bend

choices.why: context is prison and crowd enforcement, not generic persecution; the word marks men who hunt and seize rather than soldiers in rank
garment around the neck that can be tightened to choke must be a loose head-covering or mantle worn by Pionius, not a cloak clasp
adverbial phrase describes the manner of carrying a resisting man who has thrown himself down, not a wound to the head
